body:
Hey @rayrutjes, sorry for the delay.

> Could you give an example?

The issue we previously had with the currentRefined widget in InstantSearch V1 is that it had to infer which refinements were applied only from the SearchParameters. While this is possible, the result isn't always very human friendly. See the first example of #1170. Now, using only the SearchParameters, the widgets we currently have could still infer and declare their current filters from the SearchParameters.

The issue arises when two or more widgets operate on the same part of the SearchParameters, for instance a numeric refinement on the price facet. Should interacting with one widget affect the other as well? When a numeric refinement is set, should we show a current filter for both widgets? 

> What is it you call virtual widgets? widgets that have no UI?

Virtual widgets are widgets that are declared in JSX but have no DOM representation. They only exist to provide a nice way to interact with the underlying SearchParameters using the same interface as normal widgets.

> Regarding default widget state, IMHO widgets should take their state from the helper. When no state matched, then it can suggest its own default state but set it on the helper, not just internally.

We don't want default state to directly affect the helper's state, because default state should not appear in the URL. Also, we're mostly using the `SearchParameters` internally anyway, since we heavily rely on immutability in order to batch state modifications. We're only really using the helper's `searchOnce` method.
